title: Spanish Verb Querer Practice: Forms, Uses and Self-Correcting Quiz
description: Practice the Spanish verb querer: e-ie present forms, the preterite, wanting and loving, ten questions that correct themselves and a short reading. Free.
intro: Querer means «to want» and, with people, «to love». It changes e to ie in the present. Learn its forms, the difference between querer and amar, and practice with instant feedback.

demand.source: Google autocomplete for US searchers (hl=en, gl=us), docs/seo-plan/us1000/suggest-us-20261127.csv

uses.use: Wanting to do something: querer + infinitive
uses.meaning: We want to travel to Colombia.
I love you a lot, Grandma.

uses.use: Wanting someone else to do something: querer que + subjunctive
uses.example: Mi mamá quiere que estudie más.
uses.meaning: My mom wants me to study more.

uses.example: No quiso venir a la fiesta.
uses.meaning: He refused to come to the party.

quiz.why: Love for family and friends: te quiero.
Querer que + another person takes the subjunctive: leamos.
No quiso: he refused, one time.

paragraphs: Faltan dos semanas para el cumpleaños de mi mamá y mi hermano y yo queremos darle algo especial. Mi hermano quiere comprarle un teléfono nuevo, pero yo no quiero gastar tanto dinero. Además, mi mamá siempre dice que no quiere cosas caras: quiere pasar tiempo con nosotros.

Al final decidimos hacer un álbum con fotos de la familia. Le pedimos a mi papá las fotos viejas, pero al principio no quiso dárnoslas porque quería que fuera una sorpresa para él también. Cuando mi mamá abrió el regalo, lloró y dijo: «Los quiero muchísimo».

comprehension.why: She wants to spend time with them.

comprehension.before: Al principio el papá no quiso
comprehension.why: He did not want to give them the old photos.

mistakes.why: Querer que + a different subject takes the subjunctive.
Querer changes e to ie in every present form except nosotros.
Amar is very intense; te quiero is the normal way to say «I love you» to family and friends.

heritage: Heritage speakers often know te quiero and te amo by feeling. In writing, check «quiso» and «quise» with s, not z, and remember that «quisistes» is a spoken form: the written tú preterite is quisiste. Write a short message to someone you love using querer three different ways.
teacher: Teachers: the reading invites a quick discussion about gifts. Students write what they want for their birthday and what a family member wants, with querer + noun and querer + infinitive. Advanced classes can add querer que + subjunctive.

figure.text: On 27 November 2026, Google suggested 9 searches to people in the United States who typed «spanish verb querer». 4 of them ask for conjugation, charts or tenses (conjugation, present tense, past tense, conjugation chart). This page adds what a conjugation chart leaves out: when querer means love, and querer que + subjunctive.
